record.original_question: Does every 2-connected graph have an embedding in which every face boundary is a simple cycle?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.2 Every 2-connected graph has an embedding in which each face is bounded by a simple cycle.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A 2-cell embedding of a finite graph $G$ in a closed surface $\Sigma$ is an embedding $G \hookrightarrow \Sigma$ such that every connected component of $\Sigma \setminus G$ (a face) is homeomorphic to an open disk. The boundary walk of a face is the closed walk in $G$ traced by its boundary. Say that an embedding is a circular (or strong) embedding if, for every face, this boundary walk is a simple cycle of $G$ (no repeated vertices or edges).

Prove or disprove: every 2-connected finite graph $G$ admits a 2-cell embedding in some closed surface such that the boundary of every face is a simple cycle of $G$.
artifact.category_tag: Topological graph theory / strong embedding conjecture
artifact.status_search_result: The statement is the well-known Strong (Circular) Embedding Conjecture in topological graph theory. It is listed as an open problem on the Open Problem Garden and on West's open-problem list, and surveys of the cycle double cover conjecture (which it implies) continue to treat it as unresolved.
